note: The council a municipality has by its state's law for its class (borough, village, city, town), where the town's own charter has not been read. The class is the kind the Census Government Units listing names the government by ("BOROUGH OF BLOOMSBURY" is a borough). Each class says the council's seats, how long a member serves, whether the seats take turns (some up at each regular election) and whether the chief executive is elected by the voters, with the statute quoted. A town that changed its council by its own ordinance, referendum or charter is not read here and takes its class's law: a known gap until its own reading. A class not listed takes the national typical council (typical-council-size.ts).

borough.citation: N.J.S.A. 40A:60-2: "The mayor shall be elected by the voters of the municipality at large and serve for a term of four years"; "The council shall consist of six members, elected at large, and shall serve for a term of three years"; "Their terms shall be arranged, by lot if necessary, so that the terms of two councilmen shall expire at the end of each year".

8 Pa.C.S. § 806(a): "in boroughs not divided into wards, seven members of council" and "A mayor, who shall be elected at municipal elections every four years"; § 811: "Biennially, at the municipal election, a sufficient number of members of council shall be elected", each "for a term of four years". A borough of 3,000 or fewer may reduce its council to five or three by petition and court order (§ 818), and a borough divided into wards elects by ward: neither is read.

village.citation: N.Y. Village Law § 3-301(1): every village has "a mayor" and "four trustees, except that the board of trustees of a village may change the number of trustees"; § 3-301(3): "The mayor, trustees and village justices shall be elective officers"; § 3-302(3): "the term of office of mayor, each trustee, treasurer and clerk shall be two official years". A village may extend terms to four years (§ 3-302(5)): not read. Whether trustees' terms take turns is not stated; they are taken to, half up each year, as the two-year term with annual village elections gives.

65 ILCS 5/3.1-25-5: "the electors of the village shall elect 6 trustees"; "The term of office of the trustees shall be 4 years"; trustees elected at a village's first election "shall by lot designate one-half of their number, whose terms shall be 2 years", so half the board is elected at each general municipal election. A village under 5,000 may reduce its board to 4 by referendum (3.1-25-10): not read. The president's term is not read here.

Wis. Stat. § 61.20(1): "Villages shall have 6 trustees, except as provided otherwise in sub. (3)", "whose term of office shall be 2 years, 3 of whom shall be elected each year"; § 61.19: "At the annual spring election in each village in odd-numbered years" the electors choose "A president". A village of 350 or less has 2 trustees (§ 61.20(3)) and any village may change the number by ordinance (§ 61.20(4)): neither is read.
